frontMatter.welcome:
Dear Priya Associates Team Member,
It is with great pride and warmth that we welcome you to Priya Associates a firm built on trust, hard work, and a deep connection to Kerala's natural rubber heartland. Headquartered in Irrity, Kannur, one of Kerala's most productive rubber-growing regions, we have established ourselves as a dependable name in the procurement and supply of natural rubber to manufacturers across India.
Kannur district is home to thousands of rubber smallholders who depend on a transparent and fair supply chain. Priya Associates plays a vital role in this ecosystem: we procure natural rubber from growers and farmers, ensure proper grading and storage at our warehouse in Kelanpeedika, Kunnoth, and supply consistently high-quality rubber to industrial manufacturers in the automotive, footwear, engineering, and allied sectors.
At the heart of our success are our people. Whether you are involved in procurement, quality grading, warehouse operations, logistics, sales, or administration your contribution keeps this supply chain running. You are not just an employee; you are a key partner in our business and a representative of our values in the marketplace.
This Employee Handbook has been designed as your comprehensive guide to everything you need to know about working at Priya Associates. It covers our policies, your rights and responsibilities, the benefits we offer, the standards we uphold, and the processes through which you can raise concerns or seek support. We strongly encourage you to read it carefully, ask questions where anything is unclear, and refer back to it whenever needed.
We believe in a workplace where every individual is treated with fairness, dignity, and respect regardless of their designation, gender, religion, caste, or background. We are
frontMatter.about:
Priya Associates is a Kerala-based firm engaged in the procurement, storage, grading, and supply of natural rubber to industrial manufacturers. The company operates from Irrity, Kannur a town situated within one of India's most significant natural rubber-producing zones. With a dedicated warehouse and storage unit at Kelanpeedika, Kunnoth, Kannur, we are strategically positioned to source rubber from the surrounding plantation belt and ensure its timely dispatch to buyers.
Natural rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) is a critical industrial raw material used across a wide range of industries including automotive tyres and tubes, footwear, medical devices, engineering goods, construction materials, adhesives, and consumer products. India is among the world's top producers of natural rubber, with Kerala contributing the largest share. Priya Associates operates at the heart of this supply chain.
[table]
| Sr. No. | Entity | Unit Name | Registered Address |
| 1 | Priya Associates | Head Office | Building No.: PP XIII 295, Irrity P O, Kannur, Kerala – 670703 |
| 2 | Priya Associates | Warehouse / Storage Unit 1 | Kelanpeedika, Kunnoth, Kannur, Kerala – 670706 |
Our core business activities include:
- Rubber Procurement: We source natural rubber primarily in RSS (Ribbed Smoked Sheet) grades, latex concentrate, and field-grade forms directly from rubber smallholders, farmers, and local dealers in the Kannur and Kasaragod rubber belt.
- Quality Grading and Inspection: Incoming rubber is graded against standard quality parameters before storage or dispatch to ensure that buyers receive consistent, specification-compliant material.
- Storage and Warehousing: Our warehouse at Kelanpeedika provides secure, well-maintained storage for rubber stocks, equipped to prevent quality deterioration

chapters.title: Code of Conduct
chapters.text:
## Standards of Professional Behaviour
All employees of Priya Associates are expected to conduct themselves in a professional, ethical, and respectful manner at all times. The following standards apply at the workplace, at the warehouse, during field visits, and in all business interactions:
- Honesty and Integrity: Act with honesty in all dealings with colleagues, suppliers, buyers, and management. Do not misrepresent facts, forge records, or engage in any form of deceit.
- Respect and Courtesy: Treat every person regardless of their designation, gender, religion, caste, or background — with courtesy and dignity. Maintain a collegial and cooperative work environment.
- Confidentiality: Protect all confidential business information including supplier contacts, buyer relationships, pricing, stock data, and trade practices. Do not share such information with unauthorized persons inside or outside the company.
- Responsible Use of Company Assets: Use company property vehicles, equipment, rubber stocks, cash, and office resources only for authorized business purposes. Report any damage, loss, or misuse immediately.
- Conflict of Interest: Disclose any personal relationship or financial interest that could or could appear to influence a business decision. Avoid situations where your personal interests conflict with those of the company.
- Compliance with Law: Comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies at all times. If you are uncertain whether a particular action is permissible, ask your supervisor before proceeding.
- Representing the Company: When dealing with farmers, buyers, government officials, or the public, remember that you represent Priya Associates. Conduct yourself in a manner that upholds the company's reputation.
## Social Media and Communication
Employees must not post or share any confidential business information, financial data, client or supplier details, or internal company communications on social media or any public platform. Any public communication on behalf of Priya Associates must be approved by management in advance.

chapters.title: Conflict of Interest — Specific Guidance
chapters.text:
The following situations constitute a potential conflict of interest and must be disclosed to management promptly:
- Having a direct or indirect financial interest in any supplier, buyer, or competitor of Priya Associates
- Conducting personal rubber trading on the side that competes with Priya Associates' business
- Receiving gifts, commissions, or benefits from suppliers or buyers beyond what is reasonable and customary
- Having a family member or close associate employed by a supplier, buyer, or competitor
Disclosure of a potential conflict does not automatically result in disciplinary action; however, failure to disclose a known conflict of interest is a serious breach of this Code of Conduct.
## Employment Terms and Conditions

chapters.title: Recruitment and Selection Procedure
chapters.text:
Priya Associates follows a structured, fair, and non-discriminatory recruitment process. Every vacancy is filled based on the skills and qualifications required for the role. The following table describes each phase of the recruitment and hiring process:
[table]
| Phase | Key Activities | Timeline | Responsible |
| Vacancy Identification | Proprietor/Management identifies staffing requirement and prepares a job descrip | As needed | Proprietor / Manager |
| Job Communication | Vacancy shared via notice board, word-of-mouth, local newspaper, or referral net | 2–3 days | Manager |
| Application Review | Applications/CVs screened against minimum required qualifications and experience | 3–5 days | Manager |
| Interview | Structured one-on-one or panel interview; questions based on job-relevant compet | 1 week | Proprietor / Manager |
| Reference Check | Previous employer or character references verified for shortlisted candidates | 2–3 days | Manager |
| Medical Fitness | Basic medical fitness check for warehouse/physical roles (at company's expense) | 1–2 days | Manager |
| Offer Letter | Formal written offer issued to selected candidate detailing role, salary, and te | 1–2 days | Proprietor |
| Document Collection | Employee submits required documents (ID, age proof, PAN, bank details, photograp | Day 1 | Manager |
| Orientation | New employee introduced to team, policies, workplace, and safety procedures | Day 1 | Manager / Supervisor |
Priya Associates does not charge any recruitment fee to candidates. Intermediaries or agents acting on behalf of the company are also prohibited from charging fees to job seekers.
## Offer Letters and Employment Contracts
## Offer Letter
Every selected candidate will receive a formal Offer Letter / Appointment Letter before commencing work. The letter will be issued in writing and will clearly state:
- Full name and designation of the employee
- Place of posting (Head Office, Irrity or Warehouse, Kunnoth)
- Date of commencement of employment
- Probationary period (if applicable)
- Gross monthly salary and key components
- Standard working hours and days
- Notice period applicable upon resignation or termination
- Reference to this Employee Handbook and the company's Code of Conduct
The offer letter will be prepared in English or Malayalam as preferred by the employee and will be signed by the proprietor or authorized representative. The employee is required to sign and return a copy as acknowledgment of acceptance.
## Employment Contract for Contractual / Seasonal Staff
For employees engaged on a fixed-term, contractual, or seasonal basis (which is common in the rubber trade during peak harvest and supply seasons), a written fixed-term contract will be issued detailing the specific duration, terms of engagement, daily or weekly wages, and the basis for renewal or separation.
## No Verbal Commitments
No verbal promise, informal communication, or handshake agreement shall be treated as a binding employment commitment. All employment terms and conditions are governed solely by the written Offer Letter / Appointment Letter and this Employee Handbook.
## Probation Period
All newly appointed employees undergo a probationary period as follows:
[table]
| Category of Employee | Probation Period | Notice During Probation | Review |
| Permanent/Full-Time Employee | 3 months | 1 month by either party | End-of-probation performance review by manager |
| Contractual / Seasonal Employee | As per contract (if any) | As specified in contract | End-of-contract review |
| Warehouse / Operations Staff | 3 months | 1 month by either party | Assessment by warehouse in-charge |
During the probation period, the employee's performance, conduct, attendance, and suitability for the role will be assessed. At the end of the probationary period, the employee will be:
- Confirmed as a permanent employee if performance is satisfactory
- Extended for a further probation period (maximum 3 months) if performance needs improvement, with written feedback
- Released from employment if performance is found unsatisfactory, subject to applicable laws
An employee on probation is entitled to all statutory benefits (EPF, ESI, minimum wages) and the leave entitlements specified in this Handbook.

chapters.title: Working Hours and Attendance
chapters.text:
## Standard Working Hours
[table]
| Location | Working Days | Working Hours | Lunch Break |
| Head Office (Irrity) | Monday to Saturday | 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM | 1:00 PM – 2:00 PM |
| Warehouse / Storage (Kunnoth) | Monday to Saturday | 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM | 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM |
| Sunday | Weekly Off | — | Unless specifically required for operations |
| Public Holidays | As per Kerala Public Holiday list | Off | Paid holiday |
Total working hours per day (excluding the lunch break) are 8 hours. Employees are expected to arrive on time and remain at their designated work station or area throughout working hours. Late arrival without prior intimation may be noted and will be addressed through the attendance management process.
## Attendance Tracking
Attendance is recorded daily through an attendance register maintained at each location (head office and warehouse). Employees are required to:
- Sign in the attendance register at the start of each working day
- Sign out at the end of the working day
- Record any departure from the premises during working hours with supervisor's knowledge
Absence without prior notification or approval will be treated as Unauthorized Absence and may result in a deduction of wages for the absent day(s) as well as disciplinary action for repeated occurrences.

chapters.title: Overtime
chapters.text:
Overtime is work performed beyond the standard 8-hour working day or beyond 48 hours per week. Overtime at Priya Associates is subject to the following rules:
- Overtime must be authorized in advance by the supervisor or manager
- Employees required to work overtime will be compensated at double the ordinary rate of wages per hour, in compliance with the applicable Shops and Commercial Establishments Act (Kerala)
- Overtime shall not be excessive and shall not exceed the limits prescribed under applicable labour law
- Alternatively, with the employee's written consent, overtime may be compensated through Compensatory Off — one day off for every equivalent day of overtime worked — to be availed within 30 days
- Overtime records are maintained separately and reviewed monthly
## Absence Reporting
If an employee is unable to attend work, they must:
- Inform their supervisor by phone or message before the start of the working day, or as early as possible.
- Submit a written leave application (or fill the leave form available at the office) on the day of return.
- Provide a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner for sick leave exceeding 3 consecutive working days.
Repeated unplanned absences without valid reason will be addressed through the disciplinary process.
## Age Verification and Child Labour Prevention
Priya Associates strictly prohibits the employment of any person below 18 years of age in any capacity — permanent, contractual, seasonal, or casual. This prohibition applies to all locations including the head office and the warehouse, as well as to any contractors or labour contractors engaged by Priya Associates.
## Mandatory Age Verification Documents
Before an employee commences work, the following age-proof documents must be submitted and verified:
[table]
| Document Type | Examples Accepted |
| Government-issued ID with date of birth | Aadhaar Card, Passport, Voter ID, Driving Licence |
| Educational qualification certificates | SSLC/Class 10 Marksheet, School Leaving Certificate |
| Birth certificate | Issued by Municipal Corporation / Gram Panchayat |
| Medical certificate (age estimation) | If no documentary proof is available — from a registered Government Medical Offi |
If only the year of birth is available in any document (without day and month), the first of July of that birth year will be recorded as the employee's date of birth for company records.
No employee will be permitted to begin work until their age has been verified as 18 years or above. Signed copies of age-proof documents will be retained in the employee's personal file. Original documents will be returned to the employee immediately and will never be retained by the company.
## Supply Chain Due Diligence
In addition to our own hiring practices, Priya Associates is committed to ensuring that the rubber supply chain we participate in is free from child labour. We will:
- Communicate our zero-tolerance policy on child labour to all rubber farmers, dealers, and intermediaries who supply rubber to us
- During farm visits, remain vigilant to any visible involvement of children in rubber tapping or processing
- Refuse to source rubber from any supplier found to be using child labour, and report such instances to the relevant authorities
## Prevention of Forced Labour and Debt Bondage
Priya Associates prohibits all forms of forced labour, bonded labour, and debt bondage. This means:
- No employee shall be required to work against their free will or under threat of any penalty
- No employee's original identity documents (Aadhaar, passport, driving licence, etc.) shall ever be retained by the company
- No employee shall be required to make a financial deposit as a condition of employment
- No employee shall be required to repay recruitment or placement fees as a condition of keeping their job
- Every employee has the right to resign from employment with proper notice, as specified in this Handbook
- Contractual employees are not bound to accept renewals of their contracts
Employees who are required to work on their weekly off day (Sunday) or on a public holiday shall be entitled to Compensatory Off (Comp-Off) as follows:
[table]
| Aspect | Details |
| Eligibility | All employees required by management to work on Sunday or a public holiday |
| Entitlement | One full day Comp-Off for each day worked on a weekly off or public holiday |
| Approval | Overtime or Sunday working must be pre-authorized by the supervisor. Comp-Off mu |
| Validity | Comp-Off must be availed within 30 days of the day it was earned. Unutilized Com |
| Encashment | Comp-Off can be encashed at the time of full and final settlement if it has not  |
## Leave Application Procedure
The following procedure applies to all leave applications:
- Complete the Leave Application Form (available at the head office) or notify the supervisor in writing/verbally (for emergency leave).

chapters.title: Freedom of Movement
chapters.text:
Employees have the right to move freely within the workplace premises during working hours in the normal course of their duties. They may leave the premises during lunch breaks or at the end of the working day without restriction. Movement restrictions, if any, are limited to safety-sensitive areas of the warehouse and are communicated clearly to all employees.
## Right to Organize
Priya Associates respects the right of employees to join or form trade unions or workers' associations and to engage in collective bargaining in accordance with applicable Indian law. Employees who exercise this right shall not be subject to any adverse action, discrimination, or intimidation.
## Promotion and Internal Mobility
Promotions at Priya Associates are based on merit, demonstrated performance, reliability, and the operational needs of the business. The following promotion process applies:
[table]
| Stage | Description |
| Performance Review | Annual performance appraisal forms the basis for promotion consideration (see Se |
| Skill Assessment | Employee's current skill level and readiness for the new role is assessed |
| Position Availability | Promotion is contingent upon the availability of a higher position or expanded r |
| Management Decision | Final promotion decision is made by the proprietor, free from any discrimination |
| Formal Notification | Promoted employee receives a revised Appointment Letter with updated designation |
Internal transfers between the head office and the warehouse may be initiated by management based on operational requirements or at the employee's request. Employees will be given at least 2 weeks' written notice before any company-initiated transfer.
## Compensation and Benefits
## Wage Equality Commitment
Priya Associates is committed to providing equal remuneration for work of equal value, in compliance with the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976. Compensation is determined by the nature of the role, the skills and experience required, the level of responsibility, and applicable statutory minimum wages — not by gender, caste, religion, or any other personal characteristic.
The company conducts an annual review of its pay practices to identify and correct any unexplained pay disparities. Employees who believe they are being paid inequitably are encouraged to raise the issue through the Grievance Redressal mechanism (Section 10).
Any security arrangement at Priya Associates premises shall be based on the principles of proportionality and non-violence. Security personnel or supervisors are strictly prohibited from:
- Using physical force against any employee for any reason other than immediate self-defence
- Detaining, restraining, or confining any employee against their will
- Threatening employees with physical harm as a means of control or motivation
Any incident involving physical force or threat of force against an employee must be reported to the proprietor immediately and will be investigated.
## Right to Leave and Freedom of Resignation
Every employee has the unconditional right to resign from their position by giving the appropriate notice as specified in their appointment letter and this Handbook. No employee shall be forcibly retained or threatened with harm as a consequence of wishing to leave employment.
## Workplace Cleanliness and Housekeeping
A clean and well-organized workplace is important for safety, quality, and employee well-being. All employees are expected to:
- Keep their work area clean and free of clutter at all times
- Store rubber sheets, bales, and equipment in their designated locations in the warehouse
- Dispose of waste, rubber off-cuts, and packaging materials in the appropriate waste bins
- Report any spillage, damage, or safety hazard to the supervisor immediately
- Participate in regular cleaning and housekeeping activities as part of normal work duties
## Visitor and Vendor Management
All visitors to Priya Associates premises (including rubber farmers, buyers, transporters, and contractors) must:
- Sign the visitor register at the entrance of the head office or warehouse
- Be accompanied by a Priya Associates employee at all times within the premises
- Comply with all safety rules applicable to the premises
- Not access any area beyond what is required for their legitimate business purpose
Employees are responsible for the conduct of visitors they bring onto the premises and must ensure that no visitor has access to sensitive business information, rubber stocks, or equipment without authorization.
## Employee Health, Safety and Well-Being
The health, safety, and well-being of every employee is a core priority for Priya Associates. We are committed to providing a safe working environment, particularly at our warehouse and storage unit where rubber handling involves specific occupational risks. This section outlines our commitments, responsibilities, and the measures we have put in place.

chapters.title: Salary Structure
chapters.text:
The salary structure at Priya Associates is transparent, compliant with all statutory requirements, and designed to fairly reward the contribution of each employee. The following components may form part of an employee's total remuneration:
[table]
| Salary Component | Description | Typical Range / Basis |
| Basic Salary | Fixed core component; basis for EPF, ESI, Gratuity calculations | 40–50% of Gross Salary |
| House Rent Allowance (HRA) | Allowance to assist with accommodation costs | 20% of Basic Salary (non-metro/Kannur) |
| Conveyance Allowance | Fixed monthly amount for commuting between home and workplace | As per role; Rs. 800 – Rs. 1,500/month |
| Medical Allowance | Fixed allowance for routine medical expenses | Rs. 500 – Rs. 1,250/month |
| Special Allowance | Variable component to round off the salary package; role/performance-based | Varies by role |
| Overtime Pay | For hours beyond standard schedule (see Section 4.4.3) | Double the hourly basic wage rate |
| Festival / Bonus | Annual bonus as per the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 | Minimum 8.33% of annual basic salary |
| Gratuity | Statutory lump sum on completion of 5 years of continuous service | As per Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 |
Disclaimer: The above table is illustrative. Actual salary components and amounts for each employee are specified in their individual Appointment Letter. Amounts may vary based on the role, location, and experience of the employee.
## Statutory Deductions — EPF and ESI
Priya Associates complies fully with all statutory obligations concerning employee welfare fund contributions. The following schemes are applicable:
[table]
| Scheme | Full Name | Eligibility | Employee Contribution | Employer Contribution | Key Benefits |
| EPF | Employees' Provident Fund | Employees with Basic Salary up to Rs. 15,000/month (mandatory); voluntary for hi | 12% of Basic Salary | 12% of Basic Salary (split: 8.33% to EPS, 3.67% to EPF) | Retirement corpus, housing, medical, education advances; accumulated with intere |
| ESI | Employees' State Insurance | Employees with Gross Salary up to Rs. 21,000/month | 0.75% of Gross Salary | 3.25% of Gross Salary | Free medical care for employee and family, disability benefit, maternity benefit |
Employees can access their EPF account through the EPFO member portal (epfindia.gov.in) using their Universal Account Number (UAN). ESI beneficiaries can avail medical services at designated ESI dispensaries and hospitals in Kannur district. The company will assist employees in obtaining their UAN and ESI IP number if they do not already have one.

chapters.title: Bonus
chapters.text:
Priya Associates provides bonuses to eligible employees as per the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965. Details are as follows:
[table]
| Bonus Type | Eligibility | Amount | Payment Schedule |
| Statutory Annual Bonus | Employees who have completed 30 working days or more in the accounting year | Minimum 8.33% of annual basic salary; up to 20% linked to company profitability | Within 8 months of close of the accounting year |
| Festival Advance / Bonus | All employees | One month's basic salary (customary; subject to management discretion) | Before Onam or Diwali as applicable |
| Performance Incentive | Employees who achieve specific targets in procurement, quality, or operations | Determined by management based on individual achievement | Quarterly or annually as applicable |

chapters.title: Gratuity
chapters.text:
Gratuity is a statutory benefit payable under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, to any employee who has completed 5 or more years of continuous service with Priya Associates. The formula for calculation is:
[table]
| Gratuity Calculation Formula |
| Gratuity = (Last Drawn Basic Salary × 15 × Number of Completed Years of Service) |
## Payment Schedule
[table]
| Payment Item | Frequency | Mode | Timing |
| Monthly Salary | Monthly | Bank Transfer / Cash (with signed acknowledgment) | On or before the last working day of the month |
| Overtime Pay | Monthly | Bank Transfer / Cash | Included in the monthly salary payment |
| Annual Bonus | Annual | Bank Transfer / Cash | Within 8 months of close of accounting year |
| Festival Bonus | Annual / Biannual | Cash or Bank Transfer | Before the relevant festival |
| Gratuity | On separation (after 5 years) | Account Payee Cheque / Bank Transfer | Within 30 days of separation |
| Final Settlement | On separation | Account Payee Cheque / Bank Transfer | Within 45 days of last working day |
Pay slips will be issued to all employees every month, either in printed form or via SMS/WhatsApp confirmation, containing a clear breakdown of gross earnings, deductions, and net take-home pay.

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:
Priya Associates provides a comprehensive leave policy to support the health, well-being, and personal commitments of its employees. All leave is subject to operational requirements and must be applied for through the designated process.
## Leave Entitlement Summary
[table]
| Leave Type | Eligibility | Entitlement | Carry Forward / Encashment | Application Requirement |
| Annual Leave (Earned Leave) | All full-time employees after 6 months of service | 12 days per year (1 per month worked) | Up to 5 days carry forward; excess lapsed; eligible for encashment at separation | Apply at least 3 days in advance |
| Sick / Medical Leave | All employees from date of joining | 7 days per year | Cannot be carried forward or encashed | Inform supervisor same day; medical certificate for absence >3 days |
| Casual Leave | All employees | 5 days per year | Cannot be carried forward or encashed | Apply 1 day before planned absence; verbal notice for emergencies |
| Maternity Leave | Female employees with min. 80 days of service in last 12 months | 26 weeks (first 2 children); 12 weeks (third child onwards) | As per Maternity Benefit Act; no carry forward | Notify in writing at least 8 weeks before expected date |
| Paternity Leave | Male employees on birth or adoption of child | 5 days | Not applicable; not cashable | Apply 7 days in advance |
| Bereavement Leave | On death of immediate family member | 3 days | Not applicable | Notify supervisor immediately; submit proof if requested |
| Leave Without Pay (LWP) | All employees who have exhausted paid leave | Up to 10 days per year (subject to approval) | Not applicable | Written application to supervisor and proprietor in advance |
| Public Holidays | All employees | All official Kerala and National Public Holidays | Not applicable | Annual holiday list communicated at the start of each year |

chapters.title: Workplace Policies and Flexible Work Arrangements
chapters.text:
Priya Associates recognizes that different employees have different personal circumstances and that rigid working arrangements are not always the most productive approach. The company is committed to supporting employees in balancing their work and personal lives through flexible working arrangements, to the extent operationally feasible.
## Types of Flexible Arrangements Available
[table]
| Arrangement Type | Description | Eligibility |
| Adjusted Hours | Starting or finishing the working day at a different time from the standard sche | Administrative and support staff; subject to operational needs |
| Compressed Work Week | Completing the week's hours over fewer days (e.g., 5 days' work in 4 longer days | Administrative and support staff; requires management approval |
| Part-Time Work | Working fewer hours per day or fewer days per week | Available subject to operational requirements and business justification |
| Work from Home (Admin Roles) | Performing administrative tasks from home on specific days | Applicable only to administrative roles; not applicable to warehouse, grading, o |
| Reduced Hours (Caregiving) | Temporarily reduced hours for employees with caregiving responsibilities for you | All employees; subject to medical/caregiving proof and management approval |
## Application Process for Flexible Work
Employees wishing to apply for a flexible working arrangement should follow this process:
- Submit a written request to the supervisor and proprietor at least 4 weeks in advance.
- The request must describe the type of arrangement sought, the proposed start date and duration, and an explanation of how work responsibilities will be maintained.
- The supervisor assesses the operational impact and provides a recommendation to the proprietor within 10 working days.
- The proprietor makes a final decision and communicates it in writing.
- Approved arrangements are trialed for 3 months; after which they are formally reviewed.
Flexible working is a business accommodation, not an absolute entitlement. Arrangements may be varied or withdrawn if operational requirements change, with 2 weeks' written notice to the employee.
## Employee Responsibilities During Flexible Work
Employees working under any flexible arrangement must:
- Continue to meet all performance expectations and deadlines
- Attend all scheduled meetings, reviews, and team activities
- Be reachable during their agreed working hours
- Maintain the confidentiality and security of any company information accessed while working from home
- Comply with all company policies, including the Code of Conduct
## Workplace Security and Freedom of Movement
Priya Associates is committed to maintaining a secure and respectful workplace. The following measures are in place:
## Access Control
The warehouse and storage unit at Kelanpeedika operates with controlled access to prevent theft and to ensure the safety of rubber stocks and equipment. Employees are issued access permissions appropriate to their role. Security measures are not intended to restrict employees' freedom of movement beyond what is strictly necessary for safety or stock security purposes.

chapters.title: Fire Safety
chapters.text:
Natural rubber is a combustible material and fire prevention is a critical safety priority:
- All rubber stocks must be stored away from sources of heat, open flame, and electrical installations
- Smoking is strictly prohibited inside and within 10 metres of the warehouse
- Minimum 2 fire extinguishers (CO2 or dry powder type) are maintained at designated locations in the warehouse and are checked monthly
- Emergency evacuation routes are clearly marked and kept free of obstructions at all times
- Fire drills are conducted at least once every 6 months
- Electrical fittings and wiring are inspected annually and any faulty equipment is repaired before use
## Manual Handling and Ergonomics
Rubber sheets and bales can be heavy. To prevent musculoskeletal injuries:
- Employees are trained in safe manual handling techniques — bending at the knees, keeping the back straight, using mechanical aids where available
- Loads exceeding 25 kg should be lifted by two persons or using a trolley/forklift
- Employees engaged in repetitive manual handling are given regular rest breaks to prevent Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI)
- Workstations and work heights are adjusted where possible to reduce unnecessary bending or stretching
- Employees experiencing persistent back pain, joint pain, or other musculoskeletal symptoms should report to their supervisor; the company will arrange an ergonomic assessment and medical consultation if needed
## Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
The following PPE is provided free of charge to all employees engaged in rubber handling, grading, and storage operations:
[table]
| PPE Item | Purpose | Who Must Wear It |
| Safety footwear (closed-toe boots) | Protect against falling rubber bales or equipment | All warehouse and operations staff |
| Rubber gloves | Protect hands during grading and handling of rubber | Grading and sorting staff |
| Dust/fume mask (N95 or equivalent) | Protect against rubber dust and ammonia fumes (in latex handling areas) | Warehouse and latex handling staff |
| Safety vest / reflective jacket | Visibility during loading/unloading operations | Loading/unloading staff |
| Eye protection (goggles) | Protect against dust or splashes during chemical treatment | As required by specific tasks |
PPE must be worn correctly whenever entering the work areas for which it is required. Damaged or worn-out PPE must be reported to the supervisor and replaced promptly. Failure to use PPE without valid reason will be treated as a safety violation and addressed through the disciplinary process.
## Accident Reporting and Investigation
Any accident, injury, near-miss, or dangerous occurrence — however minor — must be reported to the supervisor immediately. The following procedure applies:
- Provide first aid to the injured person without delay. First aid kits are located at the entrance of the warehouse and at the head office reception.
- Inform the supervisor/manager immediately. If the injury is serious, call emergency services or transport the employee to the nearest hospital.
- The supervisor records the incident in the Accident Register and notifies the proprietor.
- An incident investigation is conducted within 24 hours to identify root causes and prevent recurrence.
- Corrective actions identified during the investigation are implemented and tracked.
- For accidents resulting in absence from work or serious injury, the appropriate regulatory authorities are notified as required by law.
[table]
| First Aid Locations and Emergency Contacts |
| First Aid Kit Locations: • Head Office — Irrity: At the front office • Warehouse |
## Occupational Health and Regular Health Check-Ups
Priya Associates provides or arranges for regular health check-ups for employees engaged in physically demanding or exposure-prone roles. Annual health check-ups are organized for warehouse and operations staff, covering:
- General physical examination
- Respiratory function test (for employees regularly exposed to rubber dust or fumes)
- Blood pressure and blood sugar screening
- Musculoskeletal assessment for employees engaged in heavy manual handling
The cost of annual health check-ups organized by the company is borne by the company. Employees are encouraged to avail of the ESI health facilities available to them at the ESIC dispensaries and hospitals in Kannur for all other medical needs.
## Employee Health and Well-Being Coverage
[table]
| Coverage | Eligibility | Benefit | Notes |
| ESI Medical Care | Employees earning ≤ Rs. 21,000/month gross | Full medical treatment for employee and family at ESIC facilities | Register at ESIC Kannur; obtain ESI card |
| ESI Maternity Benefit | Female employees covered under ESI | Full wages for 26 weeks maternity leave; pre/post-natal care | As per ESIC maternity benefit rules |
| ESI Disability Benefit | ESI-covered employees injured at work | Periodical cash payments during period of disability | 75% of wages for temporary disablement |
…

chapters.title: Family-Friendly Programs
chapters.text:
## Parental Leave and Support
Beyond the statutory maternity and paternity leave detailed in Section 6, Priya Associates supports employees with parenting and caregiving responsibilities through:
- Flexible working arrangements for employees returning from maternity leave (Section 7.1)
- Consideration for adjusted hours for nursing mothers for up to 15 months after the birth of a child
- Bereavement leave of 3 days for the loss of a child
- Sensitivity in scheduling for employees whose children or dependents are hospitalized or critically ill
## Care Leave for Family Emergencies
Priya Associates recognizes that caregiving extends beyond young children. Employees who need to take leave to care for a seriously ill parent, spouse, sibling, or other close family member may apply for Casual Leave or, where casual leave is exhausted, Leave Without Pay. Such requests will be considered sympathetically.
The management will organize at least one family or employee engagement activity each quarter. Activities may include:
- Onam celebrations with employees and their families
- Health and wellness camps for employees and their dependents
- Financial literacy sessions covering topics such as PF savings, insurance, and household budgeting
- Safety awareness programs for the rubber farming community and employees' families

chapters.title: Environmental Responsibility
chapters.text:
Priya Associates operates in one of India's most ecologically significant landscapes — the rubber plantation belt of northern Kerala, characterized by rich biodiversity, river systems, and a community whose livelihoods are deeply intertwined with the natural environment. We take our environmental responsibilities seriously and are committed to conducting our business in a manner that minimizes negative environmental impact and promotes sustainable practices throughout our operations.
## Environmental Policy Statement
[table]
| Priya Associates Environmental Commitment |
| Priya Associates commits to: • Conducting all operations in compliance with appl |
## Waste Management
Priya Associates generates various types of waste in its operations. The following waste management practices are mandatory:
[table]
| Waste Type | Source | Disposal / Management Method |
| Rubber off-cuts and rejected rubber | Grading and sorting operations | Collected, stored separately, and sold to recyclers or secondary processors |
| Packaging waste (gunny bags, plastic sheets) | Rubber receipt and dispatch | Segregated; gunny bags reused where possible; plastic collected for authorized r |
| Organic waste / food waste | Employee canteen / pantry | Disposed in designated organic waste bins; composted where feasible |
| Paper waste | Office operations | Minimized through digital documentation; paper waste sent for recycling |
| Hazardous waste (used oil, batteries, chemicals) | Vehicle maintenance, equipment | Stored in labelled containers; handed over to authorised hazardous waste handler |
| Wastewater from cleaning | Warehouse cleaning | Directed to proper drainage; not discharged into water bodies |
Employees are required to segregate waste at source using the designated bins provided at the head office and warehouse. Indiscriminate dumping of any waste — particularly rubber waste — in open areas, water bodies, or roadsides is strictly prohibited.
## Energy Conservation
Priya Associates takes steps to reduce energy consumption at its facilities:
- Lights, fans, and electrical equipment at the office and warehouse are switched off when not in use
- Energy-efficient LED lighting is used or progressively adopted at all locations
- Vehicles used for rubber transport and logistics are maintained to ensure fuel efficiency
- Unnecessary engine idling of vehicles at the warehouse is prohibited
- Employees are encouraged to report opportunities for energy saving to the manager
## Water Conservation
The Kannur region has abundant water resources, but freshwater conservation remains important:
- Water is not wasted during cleaning operations at the warehouse
- Leaking taps or pipes at any location are reported and repaired promptly
- Wash-down water from the warehouse is directed to a designated settling pit or drainage channel — it is not allowed to run freely or enter water courses
## Prevention of Pollution
Priya Associates is committed to preventing pollution in all its forms. Specific measures include:
- Air Quality: Burning of rubber waste, tyres, or any other material is strictly prohibited at all company premises. Vehicles and equipment are maintained to minimize emissions.
- Water Quality: No rubber processing chemicals, cleaning agents, or waste materials shall be discharged into rivers, canals, wells, or groundwater systems. All liquid waste is properly channeled.
- Soil: Rubber waste or chemical substances are not buried or dumped on open land. Storage areas are designed to prevent spillage that could contaminate soil.
- Noise: Loading and unloading activities at the warehouse are conducted during daytime working hours to avoid noise disturbance to the surrounding community.
## Sustainable Rubber Supply Chain
Priya Associates is in a unique position to positively influence environmental practices in the rubber supply chain. We promote the following among our farmer and dealer network:
- Responsible rubber tapping practices that do not over-exploit trees or cause bark damage that shortens the tree's productive life
- Avoidance of the use of prohibited chemicals or excessive chemical inputs in rubber cultivation
- Proper disposal of agricultural waste from rubber estates
- Retention of shade trees and natural vegetation within and around rubber plantations to support biodiversity
While Priya Associates cannot mandate the farming practices of independent smallholders, we engage with them constructively and prefer long-term relationships with farmers who demonstrate responsible environmental practices.
## Employee Responsibilities
Every employee is a steward of our environmental commitment. Specific employee responsibilities include:
- Following all waste segregation, disposal, and energy conservation procedures described in this section
- Reporting any environmental incident — spillage, leakage, improper disposal, or accidental pollution — to the supervisor immediately
…

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal
chapters.text:
Priya Associates is committed to addressing employee concerns fairly, promptly, and confidentially. Every employee has the right to raise a grievance without fear of retaliation, and every grievance raised in good faith will be taken seriously and resolved through the structured process described in this section.
## Types of Grievances
Employees may raise grievances on any of the following matters, among others:
[table]
| Labour & Human Rights Issues | Ethics & Other Workplace Issues |
| Child labour or forced labour concerns | Workplace violence or threatening behaviour |
| Harassment, discrimination, or bullying | Maternity benefit-related grievances |
| Breach of workplace ethics or Code of Conduct | Disputes over pay, overtime, or leave |
| Occupational health and safety issues | Concerns about performance appraisal fairness |
| Working condition concerns | Fraud, theft, or unethical practices |
| Violations of human rights | Environmental safety or pollution concerns |
[table]
| Step | Action | Timeline | By Whom |
| Step 1 – Submission | Employee submits grievance in writing (or verbally if unable to write) to superv | Within 5 working days of the incident | Employee |
| Step 2 – Acknowledgment | Supervisor / Manager acknowledges receipt of the grievance in writing. | Within 2 working days | Supervisor / Manager |
| Step 3 – Initial Review | Supervisor / Manager investigates the grievance, speaks to relevant parties, and | Within 5 working days | Supervisor / Manager |
| Step 4 – Formal Resolution | If unresolved at Step 3, the grievance is escalated to the proprietor, who condu | Within 7 working days of escalation | Proprietor |
| Step 5 – Final Decision | The proprietor issues a final written decision, including any corrective actions | Within 5 working days of formal review | Proprietor |
| Step 6 – Documentation | The grievance, investigation findings, and resolution are documented and retaine | On resolution | Manager / HR |
## Remediation Actions
Depending on the nature and findings of the grievance investigation, remediation may include one or more of the following:
## mmediate Actions
- For Safety Incidents: Remove the employee from risk; secure the affected area; provide first aid or medical attention without delay.
- For Harassment or Misconduct: Separate the complainant and respondent pending investigation; restrict access of the respondent to the complainant's work area if necessary.
- For Ethical Violations: Temporarily restrict access of the implicated person to sensitive business records or assets pending investigation.
## Corrective Actions
- For Confirmed Employee Misconduct: Issue written warning; provide retraining; in serious cases, suspend or dismiss.
- For Process or Safety Gaps: Implement procedural improvements; provide additional equipment or resources; update safety practices.
- For Policy Violations: Review and update the relevant policy; conduct team awareness session.
## Support for Affected Employees
- The affected employee is given reasonable time off (using paid leave) to recover if the incident has caused physical or psychological harm.
- Management arranges access to medical care or counselling if required.
- The employee is reassured that their employment will not be adversely affected as a result of raising the grievance.
- Regular follow-up by the manager to ensure the employee is well and the issue has not recurred.
## Protection Against Retaliation
Priya Associates guarantees that no employee will face any form of retaliation for raising a grievance in good faith. Retaliation includes:
- Unjustified dismissal, demotion, or denial of promotion
- Reduction in pay, benefits, or working hours
- Hostile behaviour, isolation, or exclusion from work activities
- Negative performance reviews unrelated to actual performance
- Any other adverse treatment connected to the filing of a grievance
Retaliation is itself a serious disciplinary offence and will be investigated and actioned accordingly. Any employee who believes they are being retaliated against should report it immediately to the proprietor.
## Anonymous Reporting
Employees who prefer to raise concerns anonymously may do so by placing a written note (without name) in the Grievance Box maintained at the head office. Anonymous grievances will be reviewed and acted upon to the extent possible. Employees who choose anonymity should be aware that this may limit the extent of the investigation.
## External Escalation
If an employee is not satisfied with the resolution provided through the internal Grievance Redressal process, they retain the right to approach any of the following external authorities:
- The Labour Commissioner, Kannur
- The Inspector of Shops and Commercial Establishments (Kerala)
- The Regional Provident Fund Commissioner (for EPF-related disputes)
- The Regional Director, ESIC (for ESI-related disputes)
- The appropriate civil or criminal court
…

chapters.title: Performance Management
chapters.text:
Priya Associates believes that a structured performance management process is essential to recognizing and rewarding good performance, identifying areas for growth, and aligning individual efforts with the goals of the business. Our approach is based on fairness, transparency, and constructive dialogue.
[table]
| Stage | Timing | Activities | Participants |
| Goal Setting | Start of each calendar year (January) | Employee and supervisor jointly set 3–5 key performance objectives relevant to t | Employee + Supervisor |
| Mid-Year Check-In | June–July | Informal review of progress against goals; adjust objectives if circumstances ha | Employee + Supervisor |
| Annual Review | December | Formal performance evaluation against agreed KPIs; self-assessment by employee;  | Employee + Supervisor + Proprietor |
| Feedback Session | December–January | One-on-one meeting to discuss evaluation results; recognition of achievements; d | Employee + Supervisor |
| Goal Setting (Next Year) | January | New objectives set for the coming year, incorporating previous year's learnings  | Employee + Supervisor |
## Performance Rating Framework
[table]
| Rating | Description | Implications |
| Exceptional | Employee consistently exceeds all performance expectations; demonstrates leaders | Fast-track consideration for promotion; higher performance incentive |
| Meets Expectations | Employee meets all or most performance objectives; is reliable and contributes p | Standard increment and bonus consideration |
| Needs Improvement | Employee partially meets objectives; some performance gaps exist that need to be | Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) issued; enhanced supervision and support prov |
| Unsatisfactory | Employee consistently fails to meet minimum expectations despite support | Disciplinary action; continued employment reviewed |
## Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)
If an employee's performance is rated as 'Needs Improvement', a formal Performance Improvement Plan will be developed. The PIP will:
- Clearly describe the specific performance gaps, with examples
- Set measurable improvement targets and a timeline (typically 60–90 days)
- Specify the support, training, and resources the company will provide
- Establish regular check-in points to assess progress
- State the consequences if performance does not improve to the required level
The PIP is a supportive tool, not a punitive one. Its purpose is to help the employee succeed. The employee must sign the PIP document as acknowledgment, but this does not prevent them from raising concerns through the Grievance Redressal process.
- Regular Supervisor Check-Ins: Supervisors are expected to hold brief check-in conversations with their team members at least once a fortnight to discuss progress, challenges, and support needs. These need not be formal — they may happen during the working day at the warehouse or office.
- Team Meetings: Monthly team meetings are held at each location to share business updates, safety reminders, and team feedback. Employees are encouraged to speak freely in team meetings.
- Employee Satisfaction Survey: Priya Associates conducts a biannual Employee Satisfaction Survey covering job satisfaction, working conditions, management relationships, safety, and suggestions for improvement. Surveys are anonymous and results are reviewed by management within 4 weeks. Action plans are communicated to employees.
- Suggestion Box: A suggestion box is maintained at the head office. Employees may submit written suggestions for improvements to any aspect of the business anonymously or with their name. All suggestions are reviewed by management monthly and a response is shared with the team.

chapters.title: Career Development
chapters.text:
Priya Associates is committed to helping employees build long-term careers within the organization. Career development opportunities include:
- Internal Promotion: Employees who demonstrate strong performance and develop their skills will be given priority consideration for promotions as vacancies arise.
- Role Enrichment: High-performing employees may be given expanded responsibilities — for example, a warehouse assistant may be given grading responsibilities, or a driver may be trained in logistics coordination.
- External Training Support: The company will support employees who wish to pursue relevant external training or certification courses (e.g., rubber quality testing, logistics management, first aid) by contributing to course fees or adjusting working hours to accommodate study.
- Succession Planning: The proprietor will identify one or two employees with high potential in key roles (warehouse management, procurement) and actively develop them as successors.

chapters.title: Training and Development
chapters.text:
Priya Associates is committed to the continuous learning and development of all its employees. We believe that a well-trained workforce is not only more productive, but also safer, more motivated, and better able to serve our customers and suppliers. All training programs are made available to employees on an equal and non-discriminatory basis.
## Training Categories
[table]
| Training Category | Topics Covered | Frequency | Target Audience |
| Induction / Orientation | Company overview; policies; Code of Conduct; safety procedures; role responsibil | Once — on joining | All new employees |
| Occupational Health and Safety | Fire safety; manual handling; PPE usage; accident reporting; first aid basics; e | Annual refresher; additionally on any safety incident | All employees; special focus on warehouse staff |
| Rubber Trade Skills | Rubber grading (RSS, block rubber, latex); quality parameters; stock management; | On induction; annual refresher | Procurement, grading, and warehouse staff |
| Anti-Discrimination and Harassment | Equal opportunity; POSH Act; non-discrimination; respectful workplace behaviour | On induction; annual refresher | All employees |
| Child Labour and Forced Labour Awareness | Definitions; legal framework; identification; reporting; supply chain responsibi | On induction; annually | All employees; particularly procurement staff |
| Anti-Bribery and Corruption | Company policy; what constitutes a bribe; gifts and hospitality guidelines; how  | On induction; annually | All employees |
| Environmental Responsibility | Waste segregation; energy conservation; pollution prevention; rubber waste manag | On induction; annual refresher | All employees |
| Financial Literacy for Employees | Understanding pay slips; EPF and ESI benefits; savings and insurance | Annually | All employees |
| Women's Development | Leadership skills; POSH rights and procedures; financial independence; career pl | Annually | Female employees; all employees encouraged |
| First Aid and Emergency Response | CPR basics; wound management; fire response; accident scene management | Every 2 years (with practical drill) | Designated first aiders; all warehouse staff |
## Orientation Program
Every new employee attends a structured orientation program on or before their first day. The program is conducted by the manager and covers:
- Welcome and introduction to the Priya Associates team
- Overview of the company — what we do, our locations, our customers, our suppliers
- Tour of the relevant workplace (head office and/or warehouse)
- Safety induction — fire exits, first aid locations, PPE requirements, emergency procedures
- Key policies from this Employee Handbook — Code of Conduct, leave policy, grievance procedure
- Introduction to the performance appraisal process
- Answering the new employee's questions
Each new employee is assigned a buddy (a more experienced colleague) for the first 30 days to help them settle in and answer day-to-day questions.
## Women's Development Program
Priya Associates recognizes the importance of actively developing and supporting female employees, who are often under-represented in the rubber trading sector. Our Women's Development Program includes:
- Leadership and Confidence Building: Workshops on decision-making, communication, and professional presence to help female employees take on supervisory or management roles.
- POSH Awareness: Detailed sessions on the rights of women under the POSH Act, the ICC process, and how to seek help confidently.
- Financial Independence: Training on EPF and ESI benefits, savings instruments, insurance, and household financial planning.
- Career Planning: Individual discussions between female employees and management to identify career aspirations and create a pathway for growth.
- Mentoring: Senior female employees or external mentors are paired with junior female employees for guidance and support.
## Training Records
All training activities are recorded in the Training Register maintained at the head office. For each training event, the following is recorded:
- Date of training
- Topic / training program name
- Name of trainer or resource person
- Names and signatures of all employees who attended
- Brief summary of content covered
Training records are used during performance appraisals to track individual development and to ensure that mandatory training (such as safety and anti-harassment) has been completed. Copies of training certificates or attendance sheets are retained in each employee's personal file.

chapters.title: Employee Conduct and Discipline
chapters.text:
## Standards of Conduct
All employees of Priya Associates are expected to uphold the highest standards of professional conduct at all times — whether at the head office, at the warehouse, on field visits to rubber farms, during transportation, or in any other capacity as a representative of the company. The standards described in this section, read together with the Code of Conduct in Section 3.3, define the boundaries of acceptable and unacceptable behaviour.
## Classification of Misconduct
## Minor Misconduct
Minor misconduct may result in a verbal warning for the first occurrence, a written warning for the second occurrence, or, if persisted, a final written warning. Examples include:
[table]
| No. | Example of Minor Misconduct |
| 1 | Unpunctuality or repeated late arrival to work without valid reason |
| 2 | Unexcused absence of 1–2 days without prior intimation |
| 3 | Neglect of duty or careless work that does not cause significant harm |
| 4 | Failure to maintain cleanliness at the workstation or warehouse area |
| 5 | Disrespectful or inappropriate language towards a colleague |
| 6 | Using personal mobile phone excessively during working hours in a manner that di |
| 7 | Failure to wear required PPE in a non-hazardous situation |
| 8 | Minor unauthorized use of company stationery or consumables |
| 9 | Failure to follow a minor administrative procedure or reporting requirement |
## Major Misconduct (Gross Misconduct)
Major misconduct may result in suspension pending investigation and, if proven, dismissal. No prior warning is required for major misconduct. Examples include:
[table]
| No. | Example of Major Misconduct |
| 1 | Theft, fraud, misappropriation, or dishonesty involving company property, rubber |
| 2 | Accepting or offering bribes, kickbacks, or undisclosed commissions in connectio |
| 3 | Physical assault, violent behaviour, or threatening conduct towards any person i |
| 4 | Sexual harassment of any employee, supplier, buyer, farmer, or other person |
| 5 | Willful damage to company property, rubber stocks, or equipment |
| 6 | Serious negligence causing significant financial loss, safety incident, or injur |
| 7 | Disclosure of confidential business information (supplier contacts, buyer detail |
| 8 | Forgery, falsification, or destruction of company records, invoices, or attendan |
| 9 | Working under the influence of alcohol or controlled substances during working h |
| 10 | Unauthorized engagement in a competing business activity while employed by Priya |
| 11 | Persistent insubordination — refusal to comply with reasonable lawful instructio |
| 12 | Repeated minor misconduct after receiving two written warnings within a 12-month |
## Disciplinary Action Framework
[table]
| Action Type | When Used | Process |
| Verbal Warning | First instance of minor misconduct | Issued by supervisor; note made in file; employee given opportunity to respond |
| Written Warning | Second instance of minor misconduct; or more serious minor misconduct | Issued by manager in writing; employee must acknowledge receipt; copy placed in  |
| Final Written Warning | Third instance or persistent minor misconduct; near-major misconduct | Issued by proprietor; states clearly that further misconduct will result in dism |
| Suspension (Pending Inquiry) | Alleged major misconduct (to prevent interference with investigation) | Issued in writing by proprietor; subsistence allowance paid during suspension; n |
| Demotion | Confirmed serious misconduct where dismissal is not warranted | Issued by proprietor; revised appointment letter issued |
| Dismissal | Confirmed major misconduct; repeated minor misconduct after final warning | Issued by proprietor in writing with reasons; statutory dues paid; no experience |
## Disciplinary Inquiry Procedure
Priya Associates is committed to a fair, transparent, and evidence-based disciplinary process. The following procedure applies for all disciplinary proceedings beyond a verbal warning:
- Charge Sheet: A written charge sheet is issued to the employee, clearly stating the alleged misconduct, the relevant facts, and the applicable policy or rule that has been violated. The employee is given at least 5 working days to submit a written explanation.
- Response Review: The employee's written response (if any) is reviewed. If the explanation is accepted as satisfactory, no further action is taken and no record is placed in the file.
- Hearing: If the explanation is unsatisfactory, a formal inquiry hearing is scheduled. The employee has the right to present their account, call witnesses, and, if they choose, be accompanied by a colleague. The hearing is conducted by the proprietor or a designated inquiry officer.
- Finding: Based on the evidence and the hearing, a finding is made as to whether the alleged misconduct is proven. Both parties are informed of the finding.
…

chapters.title: Whistleblower Procedure
chapters.text:
Priya Associates is committed to maintaining a culture of transparency, accountability, and ethical conduct. This Whistleblower Procedure provides a safe, confidential, and protected mechanism for any employee, contractor, or stakeholder to report concerns about unethical practices, fraud, corruption, safety violations, human rights abuses, or any other breach of company policy or applicable law.
[table]
| Whistleblower Procedure — Key Guarantees |
| 1. CONFIDENTIALITY: The identity of the person raising a concern will be protect |
## What Should Be Reported
The Whistleblower Procedure covers (but is not limited to) the following types of concerns:
[table]
| Labour & Ethics Concerns | Safety & Legal Concerns |
| Theft, fraud, or financial irregularity | Health and safety violations |
| Bribery or corruption | Environmental breaches or pollution |
| Child labour or forced labour | Discrimination or harassment |
| Sexual harassment | Misuse of company assets |
| Workplace violence or threats | Violations of applicable laws |
| Falsification of records or documents | Any other serious unethical conduct |
Concerns about matters that are primarily personal disagreements or interpersonal conflicts (as opposed to genuine ethical or legal violations) should be addressed through the Grievance Redressal process in Section 10, not through this Whistleblower Procedure.
## Reporting Channels
[table]
| Channel | How to Use | Anonymity |
| Direct report to Proprietor | Visit or call the proprietor directly; or submit a written letter/note | Name required unless submitted in sealed envelope |
| Written report to Manager | Submit a written letter or signed note to the manager at either location | Name required unless submitted in sealed envelope |
| Grievance / Whistleblower Box | Place a written note (with or without name) in the locked suggestion/grievance b | Full anonymity available |
| Postal / Courier report | Send a sealed letter to: The Proprietor, Priya Associates, Building No. PP XIII  | Anonymous if no return address provided |
| Third-party trusted colleague | Speak to a trusted senior employee who will escalate to management on your behal | Available |
## Information to Include in a Report
When raising a concern, it is helpful (though not mandatory) to include as much of the following information as possible:
- A clear description of the concern or incident
- The names of the individuals involved (if known)
- The date(s) and location(s) of the incident(s)
- Whether the concern is ongoing or has already occurred
- Any documentary evidence, if available (invoices, photos, records)
- The names of any witnesses, if applicable
Anonymous reports with minimal information may be more difficult to investigate. Providing contact details — even confidentially — enables the investigator to seek clarification.
## Investigation Process
[table]
| Step | Action | Timeline |
| Acknowledgment | All concerns (except fully anonymous ones with no contact details) will be ackno | 3 working days |
| Preliminary Assessment | The proprietor or a designated person conducts an initial assessment to determin | Within 5 working days |
| Full Investigation | A thorough investigation is conducted by the proprietor or, for matters involvin | Within 30 working days |
| Finding and Action | Findings are documented. If the concern is substantiated, appropriate corrective | Within 5 working days of investigation completion |
| Outcome Communication | The person who raised the concern is informed of the outcome and any actions tak | Promptly after conclusion |
## Protection Against Retaliation
Any employee, supervisor, or other person who retaliates against a whistleblower — for any reason connected to the concern raised — will be subject to immediate disciplinary action up to and including dismissal. Retaliation includes:
- Dismissal, demotion, or suspension connected to the raising of a concern
- Reduction in pay, hours, or benefits
- Exclusion, isolation, or hostility in the workplace
- Negative performance ratings unrelated to actual performance
- Any other adverse treatment connected to the whistleblowing
An employee who believes they are being retaliated against should report this to the proprietor immediately, or to an external authority if the retaliation involves the proprietor.
## False Reports
This Procedure is intended for genuine concerns raised in good faith — even if the concern ultimately proves unfounded after investigation. However, deliberately false reports made with malicious intent to harm another person will be treated as major misconduct and subject to disciplinary action.

chapters.title: Exit Policies
chapters.text:
An employee who wishes to resign from their employment at Priya Associates must follow the procedure below:
- Written Resignation: Submit a written resignation letter to the immediate supervisor or proprietor. The letter should state the last intended working day.
- Notice Period: Employees are required to serve the notice period specified in their Appointment Letter. Standard notice periods are as follows:
[table]
| Category | Notice Period | Notice by Company |
| Employees on probation | 1 calendar month |
| Permanent/confirmed employees (up to 1 year of service) | 1 calendar month |
| Permanent employees (more than 1 year of service) | 1 calendar month | 1 calendar month (or as per Industrial Disputes Act for workers) |
| Senior / key roles (as specified in appointment letter) | As per appointment letter |
- Payment in Lieu of Notice: Management may, at its discretion, accept payment of basic salary in lieu of the notice period — either by the employee (if they wish to leave earlier) or by the company (if it requires the employee to leave earlier).
- Acceptance of Resignation: Management will provide written acceptance of the resignation within 5 working days.
- Handover: The employee is required to complete a proper handover of all their work, files, contacts, and responsibilities to the designated person before their last working day.
## Termination by the Company
## Termination for Cause
An employee may be dismissed for proven major misconduct following the disciplinary inquiry process described in Section 13. The employee will be:
- Informed in writing of the reasons for dismissal
- Entitled to all statutory dues (EPF, ESI, unpaid wages), even in cases of dismissal for cause
- Not entitled to gratuity if dismissed for reasons specified under the Payment of Gratuity Act (serious misconduct proven by inquiry)
## Retrenchment
In the event of retrenchment (layoff for business reasons), the following applies:
- Employees who have completed 1 or more years of continuous service are entitled to retrenchment compensation as per the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
- Retrenchment compensation = 15 days' average pay for each completed year of continuous service
- At least 1 months’ notice (or payment in lieu of notice) is provided
- The principle of 'last in, first out' is followed unless there are valid reasons for a different selection
## Termination on Death of Employee
In the unfortunate event of an employee's death, the management will handle all formalities with sensitivity. Outstanding dues will be paid to the nominated legal heir as per company records and applicable law.
## Superannuation (Retirement)
The normal retirement age at Priya Associates is 58 years. On retirement:
- The employee receives a formal farewell as per the company's tradition and recognition practice
- Gratuity, EPF, and all other dues are settled within 45 days of the last working day
- An experience certificate and service letter are issued
- Management may, at its discretion, offer re-engagement on a consultancy or fixed-term basis
## Final Settlement
Upon separation (for any reason), the following items must be returned to management before the full and final settlement is processed:
- Any company-issued mobile phone, equipment, or tools
- Any company vehicle, fuel card, or access card
- All company documents, files, and records in the employee's possession
- Any cash advance or imprest amount outstanding
The following dues will be calculated and settled:
[table]
| Settlement Item | Basis | Payment Timeline |
| Outstanding salary | Basic + allowances for days worked in the final month | On last working day |
| Earned leave encashment | Number of earned leave days outstanding × daily basic salary rate | Within 30 days of last working day |
| Gratuity (if applicable) | As per formula in Section 5.5 (minimum 5 years of service) | Within 30 days of last working day |
| EPF settlement | Employee's and employer's contributions accumulated; claim via EPFO portal using | As per EPFO process |
| Notice pay recovery | If employee did not serve notice, basic salary for shortfall in notice period is | Adjusted in final settlement |
| Any other dues or recoveries | Outstanding loans, advances, or damage to company property | Adjusted in final settlement |
The final settlement will be paid via Account Payee cheque or bank transfer. An Experience Certificate / Relieving Letter will be issued at the time of release.
## Exit Interview
All departing employees are invited to participate in a brief, confidential exit interview with the proprietor or manager before their last working day. The exit interview is an opportunity for the employee to:
- Share their honest assessment of their experience at Priya Associates
- Provide feedback on management, working conditions, and culture
- Suggest improvements for the benefit of remaining employees
…

chapters.title: Employee Records
chapters.text:
Priya Associates maintains comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date records for all employees. These records are essential for effective HR management, statutory compliance, and resolving any disputes or claims that may arise.
## Contents of Employee Personal File
Each employee's personal file shall contain the following:
[table]
| Joining & Personal Documents | Employment History Documents |
| Appointment Letter / Offer Letter | Performance appraisal records |
| Signed copy of this Employee Handbook | Training attendance and certificates |
| ID and age-proof documents (copies) | Leave records |
| PAN Card copy | Disciplinary records (if any) |
| Bank account details | Grievance records (if any) |
| Photographs | Salary revision letters |
| Educational certificates | Resignation / Separation records |
## Confidentiality and Access
Employee records are strictly confidential. Access is restricted to:
- The proprietor or designated manager (for HR and legal purposes)
- The employee themselves (on written request, with the right to review their own file)
- Government authorities (labour inspectors, EPF/ESI officials) as required by law
No original identity documents (Aadhaar, passport, etc.) are retained in company records. Only photocopies are kept. The company does not share employee records with any third party without the employee's written consent, except as required by law.
## Document Retention Schedule
[table]
| Record Category | Examples | Retention Period | Disposal Method | Responsible Person |
| Employee Personal Files | Appointment letters, ID copies, appraisals, disciplinary records | Duration of employment + 7 years | Secure shredding | Manager / HR |

chapters.title: Data Privacy
chapters.text:
Priya Associates collects personal data from employees solely for the purposes of employment management and statutory compliance. This data is used only for those purposes and is not shared with unauthorized parties. Employees have the right to:
- Request access to their personal data held by the company
- Request correction of any inaccurate personal data
- Receive their personal data in a reasonable format upon separation from the company
Any suspected breach of employee data security (such as loss of records or unauthorized access) must be reported to the proprietor immediately for investigation and remediation.

## Frequently Asked Questions
## Q1: Who receives my salary and by when?
Your salary is paid on or before the last working day of each month, directly to your bank account or in cash (with a signed acknowledgment). A pay slip is provided every month.
## Q2: How do I apply for leave?
Fill out the Leave Application Form available at the office and submit it to your supervisor. For planned leave, apply at least 3 days (casual leave: 1 day) in advance. For emergencies, inform your supervisor by phone as early as possible and submit the form on your return.
## Q3: What is EPF and how does it benefit me?
EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) is a mandatory retirement savings scheme. Your employer contributes 12% of your basic salary and you also contribute 12%. This money accumulates in your EPF account with interest and can be withdrawn on retirement, or partially for specific purposes like housing or medical need. Access your EPF balance through the EPFO portal (epfindia.gov.in) using your UAN.
## Q4: I was asked for a bribe by an outsider. What should I do?
Refuse politely and firmly. Do not pay any bribe under any circumstances. Report the incident to the proprietor immediately. You are protected against any adverse consequence for refusing to pay a bribe.
## Q5: I witnessed a safety hazard at the warehouse. What should I do?
Report it to your supervisor or the warehouse in-charge immediately. Do not wait. If it is an immediate danger, alert all nearby colleagues first. No employee is penalized for reporting a safety hazard.
## Q6: I experienced inappropriate behaviour from a colleague. What can I do?
You can report it to your supervisor, the proprietor, or the Internal Complaints Committee (for sexual harassment). You can also place an anonymous note in the grievance box. All reports are investigated confidentially and you are fully protected from retaliation.
## Q7: Am I entitled to overtime pay?
Yes. Any work performed beyond your standard 8-hour working day must be authorized in advance by your supervisor and is compensated at double your hourly basic wage rate, or alternatively through Compensatory Off. Refer to Section 4.4.3 for details.
## Q8: What notice period must I serve if I resign?
For most employees, 1 calendar months’ notice is required. Refer to your Appointment Letter for the specific notice period applicable to your role.
## Q9: Can I raise a concern without revealing my name?
Yes. You may place a written note (without your name) in the Grievance / Whistleblower Box at the head office. Anonymous concerns will be investigated to the extent possible. Providing your name confidentially will allow us to follow up with you.
## Q10: I have a family emergency and need to take leave urgently. What do I do?
Inform your supervisor by phone or message as soon as possible. You do not need to come in person first. Submit a written leave application upon your return. Priya Associates will treat genuine family emergencies with sensitivity and understanding.
